P1.evidence: No setter on this call. Three-part frame again — 'you should get a good idea where you're at, build out what you want. There's alignment, we'll talk about the coaching, if not, that's fine as well' — with 'what's in the way' missing. Agreement given ('Okay') and the open question asked. Note the frame was preceded by a misleading answer about his own role: 'what is it you're doing for Trevor?' / 'Yeah, I just handle the onboard and stuff.'

P2.evidence: Work was probed properly and productively — 'You said something I'm interested in. You said, like, tasting things. Is part of your business, like, with food?' followed by 'is it something you have to do, like, for the business, like it's a requirement?' — which isolated the single biggest obstacle to his nutrition. Diet was asked directly ('Are you doing keto right now? Or are you off it right now?'). Age (50 in November), weight (87 kg to 80 kg), health checks and the training history were all volunteered, and injuries, sleep and energy were never asked.

P3.evidence: Not one goals question was asked. Everything that would have justified the price arrived unprompted: 'I want my children who are young, like they're toddlers... I want them to have this culture of fitness in the home', 'I feel like I'm a 25-year-old still inside. When I see the body, I'm like, nah, dude, what are you doing?', 'I work with young people, so I've got to be young. I can't be the fat guy that turns up and says he's the boss', and a three-year-old promise to himself about a rope climb. The rep's only move was to reflect the mechanism back — 'It sounds like you struggle to embed it into the lifestyle' and 'you've got six months until you're 50' — and then move to the pitch.

P4.evidence: The best root-cause work in the batch. 'Why do you feel like you didn't get the results with it?' on the year of personal training, 'It sounds like you struggle to embed it into the lifestyle. Why do you feel like that?', and the P4f move almost verbatim: 'it sounds like you could do it on your own if you really wanted to and really dedicated and really put the discipline in yourself. Why do you feel like you want the coaching?' The prospect named the gap cleanly: 'the problem is discipline and having some kind of structure with it.' The rep's one hypothesis — that work priorities crowd out training time — was wrong and the prospect corrected it, which is fine; asking open would have been better.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame, on the call in the batch most obviously set up for one. The prospect said a three-year promise to himself was 'just dragging on and it's deflating' and that he is six months from fifty. Nobody asked what the next two years look like if nothing changes, whether he is willing to settle for it, or whether he is ready to draw a line. Without it, the price landed as a cost rather than as the cheaper option.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind before presenting. The rep went from 'I feel like I understand. Everything makes sense' straight into the philosophy and then the price. Neither the belief question nor the all-in question was ever asked, so nothing was locked down and the discount ladder had to do the work instead.

P11.evidence: Close attempted — six-month recommendation, guarantee, price, then a three-month and a one-month option, with the onboarding timeline explained ('we book in your onboarding call with Trevor, that'll be on Monday'). Payment was never asked for at any of the three price points. The call ended with a WhatsApp number exchange and no booked follow-up.

objection_plays.detail: 'That's a grand a month, dude, that's so steep' with a stated expectation of EUR 200-300 a month. Two things ran: 'Is it worth it? Is the outcome worth it?' and a genuinely good direct challenge — 'you've kind of got two options. Either just carry on doing what you've been doing or you just go for it and let go... of the pride element of I can do it on my own.' Nothing else did: no finances-aside isolation, no SHOULD-I versus HOW frame, no offer to break the payment up, no cash, credit or investment questions. The play was resolved with a discount ladder instead of an open-wallet conversation.

'I really have to look at those numbers and think about it really carefully' and 'Give me a couple of days to think about it.' The pride challenge is close to the OA move about the way you have been approaching this being what brought you here, and it landed — 'Well, that's completely right.' But it came before the think-about-it, not after, and once the deferral arrived nothing ran: no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started', no 'are you sure', and no follow-up call booked.

A three-week trip to Corsica in ten days is a textbook OD trigger, and the rep ran it backwards — he agreed the timing was bad: 'you're not giving it 100% if you're on holiday, you just can't, you can maintain a little bit, but... it's up to you, man.' The script says the opposite: things never slow down, there is always another Thanksgiving, the only thing you can control is right now. He had also already told the prospect onboarding could be done before departure logic-wise on other calls, and did not do it here.

Two script gaps at once. First, a cheaper alternative that genuinely worked — himself: 'I actually got a lot more done when I was by myself.' Second, a prior paid coach who failed: a year of personal training for 'very little change', which is a trust-in-provider objection with no scripted answer. The rep addressed the first with the pride challenge and never addressed the second at all, despite it being the reason this prospect distrusts the category.

notes: Strong root-cause phase and a genuinely good direct challenge on the pride objection, sitting inside a call with no goals phase, no consequence frame, no commitment check and no ask for the money. The prospect volunteered every emotional lever a closer could want — toddlers, turning fifty, a three-year broken promise, leading a young team — and none of it was picked up, so when the price landed the only tool left was discounting. Two things to correct specifically: agreeing that a holiday is a reason to delay, and answering hesitation with a cheaper tier rather than with Phase 5.
